negative_reviews.author: Eva Cullion
negative_reviews.text: Literally shameful. Prices are extortionate, charging 30 quid for a roll and a side of kimchi. Food was mediocre at best, my friends ramen broth was powdery and tasted like rotten milk. When I was struggling to find my card, the guy serving us just hovered over the top of me staring like I was an alien?? 3 pounds for a small can, I can get a six pack for that price. DO NOT COME HERE!! GO TO THE OTHER ONE ON BATH STREET!

In northern quarter you can get 25% in taste card, and here not, I cannot understand, from now on I will go norther quarter

negative_reviews.author: Katie Mallard
negative_reviews.text:
Ramen dishes are 95% just noodles. They look pretty but with one piece of pak choi and a few thin slices of pork/chicken/tofu (our table had all three) the meal was very lacking. The markup must be immense. Recommend visiting small, independent Japanese places instead.
Service was fine.

negative_reviews.text: Atmosphere is nice along with the general look and vibe of the restaurant however I was really disappointed at how bad and stingy they were over the steak tataki. negative_reviews.author: Matt Knutson
negative_reviews.text:
The hand rolls were excellent.
However, we read that they were made table-side. Ours were not, which we thought was a little strange as everyone’s else’s were.
We asked for a glass of Sauvignon Blanc, they didn’t have any. But they said they may have the bottle. We ordered a bottle of Chablis instead and they came back over and said we’d have to drink it from Prosecco glasses as they ran out of wine glasses. Sure, we drank anyway. The people next to us ordered a bottle and theirs showed up with real wine glasses.
We asked ourselves are we getting the American treatment? No real clue if we did. Another odd thing: a woman stood in the corner the whole time and was ripping vertical video for what I can only assume was a social media post.
The food was good. Wish we had the same experience as everyone else.
